title: Does a waste that is restored relative to the mean fitness, with no forgetting clock (Heyde-Mahadevan rule), keep the fed vortices' trait cloud opening new ground?
summary: Does a waste that is restored relative to the mean fitness, with no forgetting clock (Heyde-Mahadevan rule), keep the fed vortices' trait cloud opening new ground? Proposed one-loop experiment below.
experiment: In c58's trait3d world, replace the waste's fixed decay dw by a restoration that depends on how the local eating rate compares to the domain mean (for example dW = ... + pw eat - dw W (eat_mean/max(eat_local,eps)) or a memory with dw 0 and a saturating W/(W+K)); run the waste arm and the kind-blind twin on c61's seed 6 to T=10000 with trait3c.py and score cloud radius, hull and new-ground share with vcmp.py (20261028T0700). Prediction from Heyde and Mahadevan 2026: travel without return, so new ground stays > 0.1 after t=8000.
